name: Groundnut Leaf Spot (Cercospora)
description: Fungal leaf spot diseases that are among the most widespread and damaging groundnut diseases. Early leaf spot and late leaf spot occur in all groundnut-growing regions, causing premature defoliation and significant yield reduction.
symptoms: Small circular brown to black spots on leaves (early leaf spot: upper surface)
Dark, nearly black spots on lower leaf surface (late leaf spot)
Spots coalescing causing large necrotic areas
Premature leaf drop starting from lower leaves
Reduced pod filling due to lost photosynthetic area
causes: Cercospora arachidicola (early leaf spot) and Cercosporidium personatum (late leaf spot)
Extended leaf wetness from rain, dew, or irrigation
Fungal survival on crop debris between seasons
treatments: Apply chlorothalonil or tebuconazole at first symptom appearance
Spray mancozeb at 10-14 day intervals during humid periods
Use propiconazole for both early and late leaf spot control
Apply sulfur-based fungicides in early stages
prevention: Plant resistant or tolerant groundnut varieties
Practice crop rotation with cereals or root crops
Remove and destroy crop residue after harvest
Maintain adequate plant spacing for air circulation
Use disease-free seeds treated with fungicide before planting
